uncited: A variant of SH Masking that applies a quadratic transition to suppress saturation outliers.
It is chosen when training data contains significant over- or undersaturated regions that act as outliers.
Builds on [Training Loss Computation with Huber and Masking](4765-training-loss-computation-with-huber-and-masking.md).
SH Masking was introduced in the context of differentiable volume rendering and Gaussian Splatting optimization.
